headline: Maximum grant award set at $1,500 as requests near $200,000 exceed about $60,000 available
summary: Grant requests are rated, and the median of member ratings becomes each application's score. The cap can be raised later if money is left over after all applications are rated. Before the cap vote, $340 was approved for an ad in the Reverly and a musician for the winter bazaar.
decisions: Approved $340 for an ad in the Reverly and a musician, unanimously by roll call.
Approved a $1,500 maximum for any one grant, by roll call vote.
Approved a median score of 7 for grant 155479, youth intervention with prevention.
Approved a median score of 8 for the Sundial Community Garden Restoration grant.
Approved a median score of 7 for the Stratton Players 2027 grant.
discussion: Grant cap level: Members debated whether a $1,500 cap should be lower than $3,000 or stay as it was. Some said the scoring system should not change at the last minute, while others worried about turning grants away.
Conflict of interest forms: Members asked when forms are needed. The answer was that a form is needed only when a member would personally benefit from a grant.
Stratton Players request: Members noted that the group asked for $5,000, far above the $1,500 cap, and that the cap is a small part of its $15,000 budget.
Food in grant budgets: Members said the Mass Cultural Council does not pay for food, so budgets that include refreshments may need to change if funded.
Winter bazaar vendors: Members said 27 vendors had signed up and room was left for about 30.
